stem: Which of the following is not true about globalization and its impact on india?

options.label: a
options.text: It has expanded trade in goods and services.

options.label: b
options.text: It has led to greater flow of Foreign Direct Investment.

options.label: c
options.text: Increase in exports is greater than increase in imports.

expl: In 1991, India implemented economic reforms. To bring the country’s deteriorating economy and the export–import system back on track, globalization was an essential step. Globalization expanded trade in goods and services and increased the inflow of foreign direct investment (FDI). However, the increase in imports was higher than the increase in exports; therefore, statement (c) is not true and option (c) is the correct answer.

stem:
india achieved a positive growth in the current account of the balance of payments in the year 2002-03.
Which of the following can be considered a possible explanation for this?
expl: For the given question, option (d) is the correct answer. The faster growth of merchandise imports compared to merchandise exports widened the merchandise trade deficit; however, the surplus from services helped cushion the overall trade deficit. Strong services exports helped India secure the seventh-largest share in global services exports. In addition, the net receipts under private transfers increased due to remittances received from abroad. These factors ensured that India’s current account deficit (CAD) remained relatively contained at 1.2% of GDP in the second quarter of FY 2024–25.

stem:
as per the Economic Survey, 2023, which of the following statements describe(s) the trend of Foreign Direct investment in india?
1. it has decreased due to the lower participation of the private sector.
2. it has increased compared to the pre-pandemic levels.
3. it has increased rapidly without decreasing in any Financial Year after the telecom sector was entirely reformed.
4. it has decreased due to a weak global economic situation.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
expl: With reference to the Economic Survey, 2022-23, statement 4 is true because FDI in India declined due to weak global economic conditions. All the remaining statements are false. According to the Economic Survey 2024-25, FDI recorded a revival in FY 2025, with gross FDI inflows increasing from 47.2 billion US dollars in the first eight months of FY 2024 to 55.6 billion US dollars in the corresponding period of FY 2025, i.e., a year-on-year growth of 17.9%. In the long run, India’s FDI inflows crossed the 1 trillion US dollar mark during April 2000 to September 2024, strengthening the country’s position as a safe and important global investment destination. As per the data of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), cumulative FDI inflows (including equity inflows, reinvested earnings and other capital) reached 1,033.4 billion US dollars during this period. From a sectoral perspective, the services sector continues to be the largest recipient of FDI, accounting for 19.1% of total equity inflows in the first half of FY 2025. Other important sectors attracting foreign investment include computer software and hardware (14.1%), trading (9.1%), non-conventional energy (7%), and cement and gypsum products (6.1%).

stem: Which one of the following countries is not a member of the G-8 Group?
expl: Initially, G-7 was an organization of seven industrial developed non-socialist countries, which included the USA, Canada, Germany, Britain, France, Italy and Japan. After moving towards a market-oriented economy, Russia also formally became a member of this organization in 1998. Therefore, it came to be known as G-8. It is noteworthy that at present, due to the suspension of Russia’s membership, it has again come to be known as G-7.

stem: Which of the following financial institution is not related to the World Bank Group?
expl: The World Bank Group includes five international institutions, namely— IBRD (established in 1944), International Development Association (IDA, established in 1960), International Finance Corporation (IFC, established in 1956), International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID, established in 1966), and Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA, established in 1988). Keeping in view the needs of the Asian region, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) was established in 1966 in Manila, the capital of the Philippines.

stem: W.t.o. came into existence-
expl: The World Trade Organization (WTO) was established as a result of the long negotiations of the Uruguay Round of its predecessor, GATT. The WTO was established on 1 January, 1995. The number of its members is 166.

stem: Who is known as the third pillar in international economic cooperation?
expl: In international economic cooperation, the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) are recognised as the first and second pillars. The World Trade Organization (WTO), the successor institution of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), has been accepted as the third pillar of international economic cooperation since it came into existence on 1 January, 1995.

stem: the first Director-General of the World trade organisation (World trade organisation) was—
expl: The WTO was established to replace GATT on 1 January 1995. In such a situation, Peter Sutherland, the then Director-General of GATT, was appointed as the Director-General of the WTO. However, the first duly elected Director-General of the WTO was Renato Ruggiero (1995–1999). Since the question asks only about the first head of the WTO, option (b) is correct. At present, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is the Director-General of the WTO. She is the first woman to be appointed to this post.

stem: Where is the headquarters of the i.a.a.F. located?

stem: Which of the following is the full form of PCra—
expl: The full form of PCRA is—Petroleum Conservation Research Association. PCRA was set up in 1978 as a registered society by reorganizing the Petroleum Conservation Action Group (PCAG), which was established in 1976, under the aegis of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. It works for developing and implementing strategies for energy conservation and environmental protection in various sectors of the economy, such as industry, agriculture, transport, domestic and commercial sectors.
